When these modern architectural icons op.Bauhaus building, Dessau: Walter Gropius designed this school with a glass curtain wall that wrapped the workshop wing, a bold look in its day.
When these modern architectural icons op.Villa Savoye: Le Corbusier's white villa near Paris on slim columns illustrates his 'five points' of modern architecture, including a roof garden.
When these modern architectural icons op.Guggenheim Museum, New York: Frank Lloyd Wright's spiral museum opened in October 1959, only months after he died. Visitors walk down a continuous ramp.
When these modern architectural icons op.Sydney Opera House: Danish architect Jørn Utzon quit the project in 1966, before it was done, and never saw the finished building in person.
When these modern architectural icons op.Centre Pompidou: Renzo Piano and Richard Rogers put the pipes, ducts and escalators on the outside, painted in bright colors, to free the interior.
When these modern architectural icons op.Louvre Pyramid: I. M. Pei's glass pyramid was controversial when proposed, but is now a Paris icon and the main entrance to the museum.
When these modern architectural icons op.Guggenheim Bilbao: Frank Gehry's curves, clad in titanium panels, so revitalized the Spanish city that urban planners now talk of a 'Bilbao effect'.
When these modern architectural icons op.Burj Al Arab: This sail-shaped hotel is often called a 'seven-star' hotel, though no official rating system goes beyond five. It stands on an artificial island.
When these modern architectural icons op.The Gherkin, London: Norman Foster's tower earned its nickname from its shape. Its curved glass spiral helps ventilate the building.
When these modern architectural icons op.Beijing's Bird's Nest: Swiss architects Herzog and de Meuron designed the stadium for the 2008 Olympics, with artist Ai Weiwei advising on the design.

When these famous texts were written.Epic of Gilgamesh: Written on clay tablets in cuneiform, it features a flood story that predates the Biblical Noah by centuries.
When these famous texts were written.Rigveda: The oldest of the four Vedas, it has over 1,000 hymns and was memorised and passed down orally for ages before being written.
When these famous texts were written.Iliad: Attributed to Homer, it covers only a few weeks of the Trojan War and doesn't actually include the wooden horse.
When these famous texts were written.The Art of War: Attributed to Sun Tzu, it argues that supreme excellence is winning without having to fight.
When these famous texts were written.Aeneid: Virgil reportedly asked on his deathbed that it be burned, but Emperor Augustus ordered it published.
When these famous texts were written.Kojiki: Japan's oldest surviving chronicle, it records Shinto myths and imperial genealogy.
When these famous texts were written.The Tale of Genji: Written by Murasaki Shikibu, a court lady, it is often called the world's first novel.
When these famous texts were written.Prose Edda: Icelander Snorri Sturluson wrote it, and it's our main source for Norse myths about Thor, Odin and Loki.
When these famous texts were written.Divine Comedy: Dante's trek through hell, purgatory and heaven was written in Italian rather than Latin, helping shape the language.
When these famous texts were written.Canterbury Tales: Chaucer wrote in Middle English, and the work is unfinished: he planned about 120 tales but wrote only around 24.

Lakes by maximum depth.Lake Victoria: Africa's biggest lake by area, it feeds the Nile and is surprisingly shallow for its size.
Lakes by maximum depth.Loch Ness: It holds more fresh water than all the lakes of England and Wales combined.
Lakes by maximum depth.Lake Geneva: Western Europe's largest lake is shared by Switzerland and France, and its Jet d'Eau shoots up 140 meters.
Lakes by maximum depth.Lake Superior: It is the largest freshwater lake by area and holds roughly 10 percent of the world's surface fresh water.
Lakes by maximum depth.Lake Tahoe: It is famously clear and sits high in the Sierra Nevada, the second-deepest lake in the US.
Lakes by maximum depth.Crater Lake: It sits in the caldera of a collapsed volcano, Mount Mazama, about 7,700 years ago, and is fed by no rivers.
Lakes by maximum depth.Lake Malawi: It has more fish species than any lake, including hundreds of colorful cichlids.
Lakes by maximum depth.Caspian Sea: The largest inland body of water, it is about a third as salty as the ocean.
Lakes by maximum depth.Lake Tanganyika: It is the world's longest freshwater lake and the second deepest.
Lakes by maximum depth.Lake Baikal: The deepest lake in the world holds about a fifth of the unfrozen fresh water on Earth.

US presidents from Teddy Roosevelt to JF.Theodore Roosevelt: The teddy bear is named after him: in 1902 he refused to shoot a captured bear, and at 42 he is still the youngest person to become president.
US presidents from Teddy Roosevelt to JF.William Howard Taft: He later became Chief Justice, the only person to have led both the executive and judicial branches of the US government.
US presidents from Teddy Roosevelt to JF.Woodrow Wilson: He led the country into World War I and won the 1919 Nobel Peace Prize for pushing the League of Nations, which the US never joined.
US presidents from Teddy Roosevelt to JF.Warren G. Harding: His term was overshadowed by the Teapot Dome scandal, which broke after he died in office in 1923.
US presidents from Teddy Roosevelt to JF.Calvin Coolidge: Nicknamed Silent Cal, he reportedly answered a dinner guest who bet she could get more than two words out of him with, You lose.
US presidents from Teddy Roosevelt to JF.Herbert Hoover: A mining engineer who ran massive food relief after World War I, he took office in 1929, months before the stock market crash.
US presidents from Teddy Roosevelt to JF.Franklin D. Roosevelt: The only president elected four times, he led the country through the Depression and most of World War II, dying in April 1945.
US presidents from Teddy Roosevelt to JF.Harry S. Truman: The S in his name stood for nothing: his two grandfathers' names were S-initials, so it honoured both; he ordered the atomic bombs used on Japan.
US presidents from Teddy Roosevelt to JF.Dwight D. Eisenhower: The former Allied commander in Europe launched the Interstate Highway System in 1956 and warned of a military-industrial complex.
US presidents from Teddy Roosevelt to JF.John F. Kennedy: At 43 he was the youngest person ever elected president, and he was assassinated in Dallas in November 1963.

Reptiles on the scale.Green anole: It can change from green to brown and extends a pink throat fan; it is the only native anole in the US.
Reptiles on the scale.Leopard gecko: Unlike many geckos it has eyelids and cannot climb glass, and it stores fat in its tail.
Reptiles on the scale.Bearded dragon: From Australia, it flares a spiky throat and is a popular pet.
Reptiles on the scale.Gila monster: One of the few venomous lizards, it stores fat in its tail, and a drug from its saliva inspired a diabetes treatment.
Reptiles on the scale.Green iguana: It can fall from trees and survive, and it has a third parietal eye that senses light.
Reptiles on the scale.Common snapping turtle: It cannot pull fully into its shell, hence its defensive bite.
Reptiles on the scale.Komodo dragon: The world's largest lizard has venom glands and lives only on a few Indonesian islands.
Reptiles on the scale.Green sea turtle: Adults eat seagrass, unusual for sea turtles, and its fat is green, hence the name.
Reptiles on the scale.Galápagos tortoise: Some live over 150 years, and the islands are named after them: galapago means tortoise.
Reptiles on the scale.Saltwater crocodile: The largest living reptile, males can reach up to 6 m long.

Famous popes of the past, by election.Leo the Great: He reportedly persuaded Attila the Hun to turn back from Rome in 452, and he strengthened the pope's authority.
Famous popes of the past, by election.Gregory the Great: He sent Augustine to convert England, and Gregorian chant is named after him by tradition.
Famous popes of the past, by election.Leo III: He crowned Charlemagne emperor on Christmas Day in the year 800, reviving the idea of a Roman empire in the West.
Famous popes of the past, by election.Urban II: At Clermont in 1095 he called for the First Crusade, which led to the capture of Jerusalem in 1099.
Famous popes of the past, by election.Innocent III: He held vast power, from deposing kings to calling the Fourth Lateran Council, and he approved the Franciscan order.
Famous popes of the past, by election.Boniface VIII: His clash with the French king ended with his capture, and Dante placed him in hell.
Famous popes of the past, by election.Alexander VI (Borgia): Rodrigo Borgia was the father of Cesare and Lucrezia, and he divided the New World between Spain and Portugal.
Famous popes of the past, by election.Julius II: Nicknamed the Warrior Pope, he commissioned Michelangelo to paint the Sistine Chapel ceiling and began the new St Peter's.
Famous popes of the past, by election.Leo X: A Medici who loved art and luxury, he was pope when Martin Luther posted his 95 Theses in 1517.
Famous popes of the past, by election.Pius IX: His reign of about 31 years was the longest of any elected pope, and in 1854 he defined the Immaculate Conception.

When each period film's story takes plac.300: Frank Miller's graphic novel inspired the film about Spartans at Thermopylae, where thousands of Greek allies fought beside the 300.
When each period film's story takes plac.Gladiator: Emperor Marcus Aurelius died in AD 180, succeeded by Commodus, who really fought in the arena, though Maximus is fictional.
When each period film's story takes plac.Braveheart: William Wallace was real, but the film bends history; its famous Stirling Bridge battle famously contains no bridge.
When each period film's story takes plac.The Last of the Mohicans: Based on James Fenimore Cooper's 1826 novel, it is set during the French and Indian War around the siege of Fort William Henry.
When each period film's story takes plac.Les Misérables (2012): Victor Hugo's novel runs from Waterloo's aftermath to the 1832 June Rebellion, and this film had actors sing live on set rather than lip-sync.
When each period film's story takes plac.Titanic: The real ship sank in April 1912, and director James Cameron dived to the actual wreck many times while preparing his recreation.
When each period film's story takes plac.Casablanca: Shot on a Hollywood backlot, it is set just before Pearl Harbor, and its final script pages were reportedly still being written during filming.
When each period film's story takes plac.Saving Private Ryan: Spielberg's opening recreation of Omaha Beach on D-Day runs over 20 minutes, and some veterans found it unnervingly accurate.
When each period film's story takes plac.Dirty Dancing: Set in a Catskills resort in summer 1963, it was actually filmed in Virginia and North Carolina and made an anthem of (I've Had) the Time of My Life.
When each period film's story takes plac.Apollo 13: The real astronaut's line was Houston, we've had a problem; the film changed it to Houston, we have a problem.

Not paintings: priciest auction sales.Jordan's 1998 Finals jersey: Worn in Game 1 of the 1998 Finals, the last of the Bulls' title runs, it became the best-known piece of Last Dance memorabilia.
Not paintings: priciest auction sales.1952 Topps Mickey Mantle card: Cards from this 1952 set are the hobby's holy grail, and a famous tale says Topps dumped unsold stock into the Atlantic in 1960.
Not paintings: priciest auction sales.Lady Blunt Stradivarius: Made in 1721 by Antonio Stradivari, it is named for Lady Anne Blunt, Lord Byron's granddaughter, who owned it for about 30 years.
Not paintings: priciest auction sales.Magna Carta (1297 copy): King John sealed the first Magna Carta in 1215. This 1297 version was bought by David Rubenstein, who lent it to the US National Archives.
Not paintings: priciest auction sales.Babe Ruth called-shot jersey: Ruth is said to have pointed toward the outfield before homering in the 1932 World Series, though whether he truly called it is still debated.
Not paintings: priciest auction sales.Wizard of Oz ruby slippers: Judy Garland wore several pairs in 1939. In L. Frank Baum's book they were silver, and the film changed them to ruby to flaunt Technicolor.
Not paintings: priciest auction sales.Apex the stegosaurus: This fossil, about 150 million years old and over 3 m tall, was found in Colorado, and its buyer lent it to New York's American Museum of Natural History.
Not paintings: priciest auction sales.Ferrari 250 GTO (2018 sale): Only about three dozen were built, and these racing Ferraris are widely considered the most coveted classic cars ever made.
Not paintings: priciest auction sales.The Pink Star diamond: At about 59.6 carats, this oval pink diamond was graded flawless by the GIA, and it was sold in Hong Kong in 2017.
Not paintings: priciest auction sales.Mercedes 300 SLR Uhlenhaut: Only two of these racing-derived coupes were built; Mercedes-Benz sold this one privately in 2022, at the highest price ever paid for a car.

Turning points in British history.Henry VIII breaks with Rome: Henry's Act of Supremacy made him head of the Church of England, mainly because the Pope would not annul his marriage to Catherine of Aragon.
Turning points in British history.Charles I executed: After the Civil War, Parliament tried and beheaded the king, and England briefly became a republic; he walked out to his execution wearing two shirts against the cold.
Turning points in British history.Union with Scotland: The Acts of Union merged the parliaments of England and Scotland, and the name Great Britain became a single kingdom.
Turning points in British history.Battle of Culloden: The last pitched battle fought on British soil ended the Jacobite rising in less than an hour, and left the Highlands' clan system in decline.
Turning points in British history.Union with Ireland: The Act of Union created the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, and later the Irish Free State left it in the 1920s.
Turning points in British history.Great Reform Act: It abolished so-called rotten boroughs like Old Sarum, which had almost no voters but sent MPs, and gave seats to growing cities like Manchester.
Turning points in British history.Victoria's coronation: She was crowned at 19 at Westminster Abbey, and her reign lasted so long that the age is named after her.
Turning points in British history.NHS founded: Aneurin Bevan, the Labour health minister, launched care free at the point of use, and it remains the UK's most cherished public institution.
Turning points in British history.UK joins the EEC: Britain joined after two earlier French vetoes by de Gaulle, and it would later vote to leave the successor EU in a 2016 referendum.
Turning points in British history.Channel Tunnel opens: The 50 km rail link under the sea, built with French partners, lets trains cross from London to Paris, and its two ends met in 1990 under the seabed.

Connection speeds.Dial-up modem: Its 56 kbit/s ceiling was a limit of phone lines; those screeching sounds were the modems' handshake, and the line couldn't carry a call.
Connection speeds.ISDN line: ISDN bonded two 64 kbit/s channels, and jokes said it stood for 'It Still Does Nothing'.
Connection speeds.Bluetooth 2.0 + EDR: Bluetooth is named for Harald Bluetooth, the Danish king who united warring tribes, as the tech united different devices.
Connection speeds.Wi-Fi 802.11b: The first popular Wi-Fi standard used the 2.4 GHz band, which microwave ovens can interfere with.
Connection speeds.Wi-Fi 802.11g: This 54 Mbit/s standard was backwards compatible with the slower 802.11b, which helped it spread fast in homes.
Connection speeds.USB 2.0: Launched in 2000 as 'Hi-Speed', but real transfers run well below this peak.
Connection speeds.USB 3.0: Blue plastic inside a Type-A port usually signals USB 3.0, a handy colour code for finding the faster sockets.
Connection speeds.HDMI 1.4: Version 1.4 supported 4K at 30 Hz and added an Ethernet channel, so the TV could also share an internet connection.
Connection speeds.Thunderbolt 3: It used the USB-C connector and was developed by Intel with Apple's help, so one cable can carry data, video and power.
Connection speeds.Thunderbolt 5: It can boost to 120 Gbit/s when driving high-resolution displays, which makes it far faster than any ordinary home internet link.

When these shooters came out.Wolfenstein 3D: The id Software game popularized the first-person shooter genre, and Doom soon followed, built from the same ideas.
When these shooters came out.Quake: Its fully 3D worlds and online play helped launch esports, and the mouse-look control it popularized is now standard.
When these shooters came out.GoldenEye 007: A small team at Rare, many new to games, built the console classic, and its four-player split-screen matches defined many sleepovers.
When these shooters came out.Halo: Combat Evolved: It launched the original Xbox, and Master Chief became the console's mascot, with the game ported to computers later.
When these shooters came out.Far Cry: Crytek in Germany made it, the same studio that later built Crysis, whose graphics were a benchmark for years.
When these shooters came out.BioShock: It's set in the underwater city of Rapture, and its famous Would you kindly twist reveals the player was being controlled.
When these shooters came out.Borderlands: Its cel-shaded style and billions of procedurally generated guns made loot the focus, and it helped popularize looter shooters.
When these shooters came out.Destiny: Made by Bungie, the studio behind Halo, it blended a shooter with online MMO ideas, and was famously expensive to build.
When these shooters came out.Overwatch: Blizzard's first new franchise in many years, it rose from the cancelled Titan project, and had a diverse cast of heroes.
When these shooters came out.Valorant: Riot's free-to-play tactical shooter blends gunplay with character abilities, and was first called Project A.

US Monopoly property prices.Mediterranean Avenue: The game began as the Landlord's Game, created by Lizzie Magie in 1904, and the board's streets are from Atlantic City, New Jersey.
US Monopoly property prices.Oriental Avenue: Named for a real Atlantic City street, it sits right beside a Chance space, where a card can send you across the board.
US Monopoly property prices.Connecticut Avenue: The last of the light blues, it is the property you reach just before the Jail corner.
US Monopoly property prices.Electric Company: Monopoly's two utilities pay rent according to the dice, four times or ten times what you rolled.
US Monopoly property prices.St. James Place: It is in the orange set, and orange is often named among the most-landed-on, partly because of the Jail exit.
US Monopoly property prices.Kentucky Avenue: It is part of the red set, which sits just past the Jail exit and is landed on often.
US Monopoly property prices.Atlantic Avenue: Named for the ocean beside Atlantic City, the New Jersey resort whose streets inspired the board.
US Monopoly property prices.Pennsylvania Avenue: It shares a name with Washington's famous avenue but is named for a street in Atlantic City.
US Monopoly property prices.Park Place: With Boardwalk it forms the priciest color set, and Park Place was also the name of an Atlantic City casino.
US Monopoly property prices.Boardwalk: Atlantic City's wooden Boardwalk opened in 1870 as the first of its kind in the United States.

Leonardo DiCaprio films by release.What's Eating Gilbert Grape: This film earned DiCaprio his first Oscar nomination, for playing Arnie, a boy with a developmental disability, opposite Johnny Depp.
Leonardo DiCaprio films by release.Romeo + Juliet: Baz Luhrmann set Shakespeare's tragedy in a modern city, but kept the original dialogue in the script.
Leonardo DiCaprio films by release.Titanic: James Cameron's film won 11 Oscars and stayed the highest-grossing film ever until Avatar overtook it in 2010.
Leonardo DiCaprio films by release.Catch Me If You Can: Frank Abagnale Jr. claimed to have posed as a pilot and a doctor, though parts of his story have since been questioned.
Leonardo DiCaprio films by release.The Aviator: This biopic about Howard Hughes was directed by Martin Scorsese and won five Oscars, but not for its lead.
Leonardo DiCaprio films by release.The Departed: Scorsese's crime thriller won Best Picture for 2006, and it remade the Hong Kong film Infernal Affairs.
Leonardo DiCaprio films by release.Inception: Christopher Nolan's dream-heist thriller ends on a spinning top, and fans still argue whether it falls.
Leonardo DiCaprio films by release.Django Unchained: Quentin Tarantino's Western gave DiCaprio a rare villain role, and he cut his hand on glass during the dinner scene but kept going.
Leonardo DiCaprio films by release.The Wolf of Wall Street: Scorsese's film holds a record for the number of times the F-word is used in a non-documentary film.
Leonardo DiCaprio films by release.The Revenant: This film finally won DiCaprio the Best Actor Oscar, and it was shot largely in natural light in freezing locations.

Pen names, by the writer's birth year.Molière: Real name Jean-Baptiste Poquelin, he took this name when he joined a theatre troupe.
Pen names, by the writer's birth year.Voltaire: Born Francois-Marie Arouet, he wrote Candide and was imprisoned in the Bastille.
Pen names, by the writer's birth year.Stendhal: Born Marie-Henri Beyle, he gave his name to the fainting 'Stendhal syndrome' in Florence.
Pen names, by the writer's birth year.George Eliot: Mary Ann Evans used a male name to be taken seriously; her Middlemarch is a classic.
Pen names, by the writer's birth year.Lewis Carroll: Charles Dodgson, an Oxford mathematics lecturer, wrote Alice for Alice Liddell.
Pen names, by the writer's birth year.Mark Twain: Samuel Clemens took it from a riverboat call meaning two fathoms deep.
Pen names, by the writer's birth year.O. Henry: William Sydney Porter wrote while in prison for embezzlement; he is famed for twist endings like The Gift of the Magi.
Pen names, by the writer's birth year.George Orwell: Eric Blair took the name from the River Orwell in Suffolk.
Pen names, by the writer's birth year.Dr. Seuss: Theodor Geisel wrote Green Eggs and Ham on a bet, using only 50 different words.
Pen names, by the writer's birth year.John le Carré: David Cornwell worked for MI5 and MI6, and wrote The Spy Who Came in from the Cold.

Wedding anniversaries of stones and meta.Tin: Tin is the traditional 10th-anniversary gift because it is durable yet flexible, a nod to a marriage that bends without breaking.
Wedding anniversaries of stones and meta.Crystal: Crystal suits the 15th year because clear, brilliant glass lets light shine through, much as a long marriage is meant to be transparent.
Wedding anniversaries of stones and meta.Silver: Silver became the symbol of a quarter-century of marriage in medieval Germany, where husbands crowned wives with silver wreaths.
Wedding anniversaries of stones and meta.Pearl: Pearls form when an oyster coats an irritant in layers of nacre, which makes a fitting symbol for a bond smoothed over 30 years.
Wedding anniversaries of stones and meta.Coral: Coral is an animal colony, not a stone, and its red branches were once thought to protect sailors and children from harm.
Wedding anniversaries of stones and meta.Ruby: Ruby ranks among the hardest gems after diamond, and its red glow has long stood for passion that survives four decades.
Wedding anniversaries of stones and meta.Sapphire: Sapphire is the same mineral as ruby, corundum, and gets its blue from traces of iron and titanium.
Wedding anniversaries of stones and meta.Gold: Gold is so soft and unreactive that it never tarnishes, which is why it marks half a century together.
Wedding anniversaries of stones and meta.Emerald: Emerald owes its green to chromium, and the gem is usually full of tiny flaws jardin, French for garden, that give each stone its character.
Wedding anniversaries of stones and meta.Diamond: Diamond means 'unconquerable' in its Greek root, and it is the hardest natural material, so it tops the list at 60 years.

Algorithms by time complexity.Array index lookup: Reading an array element by its index takes the same time however big the array is, as the computer jumps straight to the right address.
Algorithms by time complexity.Union-find (optimized): The inverse Ackermann function grows so slowly that, for any input that can fit in the universe, it is effectively at most 4.
Algorithms by time complexity.Binary search: It repeatedly halves the search space, so 1,000 items need around 10 steps and a billion around 30, but the list must be sorted first.
Algorithms by time complexity.Trial-division prime test: To test whether n is prime, you need only check divisors up to its square root, since any larger factor pairs with a smaller one.
Algorithms by time complexity.Linear search: It checks items one by one, and for short or unsorted lists it can beat fancier methods because it has no setup cost.
Algorithms by time complexity.Merge sort: John von Neumann invented it in 1945, and it splits the list in half, sorts each half and merges them, always in this n log n time.
Algorithms by time complexity.Bubble sort: This simple sort swaps neighbours repeatedly, and Barack Obama once joked that it was not the way to go when asked about sorting a million integers.
Algorithms by time complexity.Naive matrix multiply: The schoolbook method multiplies two n by n matrices with three nested loops, and Strassen's algorithm showed in 1969 that it can be beaten.
Algorithms by time complexity.Brute-force subset search: Checking every possible subset doubles the work with every element added, so 300 items would need more steps than there are atoms in the universe.
Algorithms by time complexity.Brute-force traveling salesman: The salesman must visit every city once, and trying every route grows as n factorial; 20 cities already give over two quintillion routes.

Milestone computers.Colossus: Built at Bletchley Park to crack German codes, this machine used about 2,400 vacuum tubes, and its existence was kept secret for decades.
Milestone computers.ENIAC: The Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer filled a large room, and it was mostly operated by six women programmers.
Milestone computers.UNIVAC I: It was the first commercial computer in the U.S. and it famously predicted the 1952 presidential election outcome on television.
Milestone computers.IBM System/360: IBM bet its future on this family of computers, whose name referred to covering all 360 degrees of uses, and it standardised the byte.
Milestone computers.Altair 8800: This kit computer, which appeared on the cover of Popular Electronics, inspired Bill Gates and Paul Allen to write BASIC for it.
Milestone computers.Cray-1: The supercomputer with a distinctive C shape and built-in bench seats was fast mainly because of its vector processing.
Milestone computers.IBM PC: IBM's first widely sold personal computer ran PC-DOS, supplied by Microsoft, and it helped set the standard for desktops.
Milestone computers.Commodore 64: This home computer is considered the best-selling single model of all time, with millions sold, and it had famous SID sound.
Milestone computers.Raspberry Pi: The credit-card-sized, cheap computer was built to teach programming, and it sold millions to hobbyists and schools.
Milestone computers.Frontier (first exascale): Located at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, it was the first computer to officially pass one quintillion calculations per second.

When these birds went extinct.Elephant bird: Madagascar's elephant birds stood about 3 m tall and laid eggs holding the volume of over 100 chicken eggs.
When these birds went extinct.Moa: The flightless moa of New Zealand had no wings at all, and Māori hunting wiped out all species within roughly two centuries.
When these birds went extinct.Dodo: Found only on Mauritius, the dodo was gone within about a century of Dutch sailors arriving, helped by introduced pigs and rats.
When these birds went extinct.Great auk: This flightless 'original penguin' of the North Atlantic was last seen alive in 1844 on an Icelandic islet, killed for collectors.
When these birds went extinct.Labrador duck: This shy sea duck of North America's Atlantic coast vanished so quietly that scientists still argue about what killed it off.
When these birds went extinct.Stephens Island wren: The only flightless songbird ever known lived on one tiny New Zealand island and is usually blamed on the lighthouse keeper's cat.
When these birds went extinct.Huia: Male and female huia had strikingly different beaks, short and straight versus long and curved. Māori prized its tail feathers.
When these birds went extinct.Passenger pigeon: Once among the most numerous birds on Earth, flocks of billions darkened the sky. The last one, Martha, died in Cincinnati Zoo.
When these birds went extinct.Carolina parakeet: The only parrot native to the eastern United States, its last captive died at Cincinnati Zoo, four years after Martha the pigeon.
When these birds went extinct.Heath hen: The last of this prairie-chicken relative was a male nicknamed Booming Ben, watched by researchers on Martha's Vineyard.

Elements by atomic number.Hydrogen: Makes up about three quarters of all ordinary matter in the universe by mass, and fuels the stars.
Elements by atomic number.Helium: It was first detected in the Sun's light in 1868, before anyone found it on Earth, and is named for the Greek word for sun.
Elements by atomic number.Carbon: The backbone of all known life, it also forms both soft graphite and hard diamond.
Elements by atomic number.Oxygen: It makes up about 21% of air but nearly half of Earth's crust by mass, locked in rocks.
Elements by atomic number.Sodium: A soft metal that fizzes violently in water, yet joins with chlorine to make ordinary table salt.
Elements by atomic number.Iron: Stars can't gain energy by fusing it, so massive stars die once their cores turn to this metal.
Elements by atomic number.Silver: The best electrical and heat conductor of all metals. Its symbol Ag comes from the Latin argentum, which also names Argentina.
Elements by atomic number.Gold: Its symbol Au comes from Latin aurum, and most of it was probably forged in neutron star collisions.
Elements by atomic number.Lead: Its symbol Pb comes from the Latin plumbum, which gave us the word plumber, since Romans piped water through it.
Elements by atomic number.Uranium: Named after the planet Uranus, it is the heaviest element found in nature in any quantity.

Ocean animals by weight.Clownfish: All clownfish are born male, and the dominant one in a group becomes female. A mucus coating protects them from anemone stings.
Ocean animals by weight.American lobster: It grows throughout its life, has blue blood, and its age is hard to determine.
Ocean animals by weight.Atlantic salmon: Salmon return to the river where they hatched to spawn, navigating by smell.
Ocean animals by weight.Giant Pacific octopus: It has three hearts and blue blood, and can squeeze through any gap larger than its beak.
Ocean animals by weight.Sea otter: It has the densest fur of any animal, roughly a million hairs per square inch, and sleeping otters hold hands.
Ocean animals by weight.Bottlenose dolphin: Each dolphin has a signature whistle that works like a name.
Ocean animals by weight.Leatherback turtle: This turtle has a leathery shell, not a hard one, and dives deeper than 1,000 m.
Ocean animals by weight.Orca: It is actually the largest dolphin, and different pods have their own dialects.
Ocean animals by weight.Whale shark: The biggest fish is a filter feeder, and its pattern of spots is unique like a fingerprint.
Ocean animals by weight.Blue whale: The largest animal known ever, bigger than any dinosaur, its call is among the loudest made by any animal.

Metric prefixes.Nano: From the Greek nanos, meaning dwarf, a nanometre is a billionth of a metre.
Metric prefixes.Micro: The Greek word mikros means small, and a micrometre is a thousandth of a millimetre.
Metric prefixes.Milli: Despite the name, millipedes rarely come close to a thousand legs, and the record, in Western Australia, is about 1,300.
Metric prefixes.Centi: The cent is a hundredth of a dollar, and the prefix also gives us the centipede.
Metric prefixes.Deci: The decibel is a tenth of a bel, a unit named after Alexander Graham Bell.
Metric prefixes.Deca: The prefix is from the Greek for ten, and gives us decade and decathlon.
Metric prefixes.Hecto: A hectare is a hundred ares, or 10,000 square metres, about the size of a rugby pitch.
Metric prefixes.Kilo: The kilogram is the only base SI unit whose name already contains a prefix.
Metric prefixes.Mega: From the Greek megas, meaning great, it also means a million in computing.
Metric prefixes.Giga: From the Greek gigas, giant, and each gigabyte holds a thousand megabytes.

When the US went to war.Revolutionary War: The war began in April 1775 at Lexington and Concord, with the famous shot heard round the world.
When the US went to war.Mexican-American War: In the 1848 treaty Mexico gave up about half its territory, including California, Nevada and Utah, to the US.
When the US went to war.Civil War: It started in April 1861 at Fort Sumter, and its roughly 620,000 deaths exceed those of any other American war.
When the US went to war.Spanish-American War: It lasted only about four months in 1898, and the US gained Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines.
When the US went to war.World War I: The US joined in April 1917 after Germany resumed unrestricted submarine warfare and the Zimmermann Telegram came to light.
When the US went to war.World War II: The US entered after Japan attacked Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941, a date Roosevelt said would live in infamy.
When the US went to war.Korean War: It was never ended by a peace treaty, only an armistice in 1953, so the two Koreas are technically still at war.
When the US went to war.Vietnam (Gulf of Tonkin): Congress never declared war; the 1964 Gulf of Tonkin Resolution let President Johnson escalate American involvement.
When the US went to war.Gulf War: In Operation Desert Storm, the ground war lasted only about 100 hours, after weeks of air strikes.
When the US went to war.Iraq War: It began in March 2003 on claims that Iraq held weapons of mass destruction, which were never found.

Volcanic islands, from oldest to newborn.Iceland: It sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge over a hot spot, where the Eurasian and North American plates slowly pull apart.
Volcanic islands, from oldest to newborn.Kauai: The oldest main Hawaiian island is also home to Mount Waiʻaleʻale, one of the rainiest places on Earth.
Volcanic islands, from oldest to newborn.Oahu: Home to Honolulu, it is built from two eroded volcanoes, and the Diamond Head crater is a famous landmark.
Volcanic islands, from oldest to newborn.Maui: Haleakalā rises over 3,000 metres above the sea and last erupted several centuries ago.
Volcanic islands, from oldest to newborn.Hawaii's Big Island: Still growing, it has Kīlauea erupting often, while an underwater volcano called Lōʻihi builds the next island to its southeast.
Volcanic islands, from oldest to newborn.Anak Krakatau: Its name means 'child of Krakatoa'; it rose from the caldera of the 1883 eruption and partly collapsed in 2018, sparking a tsunami.
Volcanic islands, from oldest to newborn.Capelinhos, Azores: An eruption off Faial lasted over a year, burying a lighthouse in ash and adding new land to the island.
Volcanic islands, from oldest to newborn.Surtsey: Named for the Norse fire giant Surtr, it is a protected site where scientists watch life colonize bare lava; visitors are banned.
Volcanic islands, from oldest to newborn.Nishinoshima's new land: An eruption off Japan's Ogasawara islands built new land that swallowed the old islet, growing it many times larger.
Volcanic islands, from oldest to newborn.Hunga Tonga–Hunga Haʻapai: The two islets merged after the 2015 eruption; in 2022 a huge explosion destroyed most of it and sent shockwaves around the planet.

Birds of prey by weight.Elf owl: The smallest owl in the world nests in woodpecker holes in giant saguaro cacti and mostly eats insects.
Birds of prey by weight.American kestrel: North America's smallest falcon hovers over fields hunting, and sees ultraviolet to follow vole trails.
Birds of prey by weight.Eurasian sparrowhawk: Females are bigger than males, and the hawk hunts by ambushing birds, darting through hedges at speed.
Birds of prey by weight.Barn owl: Its heart-shaped face channels sound so well that it can catch mice in total darkness by ear alone.
Birds of prey by weight.Red-tailed hawk: The famous "eagle scream" in movies is usually this hawk's cry, dubbed over a bald eagle's.
Birds of prey by weight.Snowy owl: Males turn whiter with age, and unlike most owls these birds hunt in daylight in the Arctic summer.
Birds of prey by weight.Eurasian eagle-owl: One of the largest owls in the world, it takes prey as big as foxes and hares, and has ear tufts that aren't ears.
Birds of prey by weight.Golden eagle: This eagle can dive at well over 100 mph, and it was once used by falconers to hunt wolves in central Asia.
Birds of prey by weight.Harpy eagle (female): Its talons are as long as a grizzly bear's claws, and it hunts sloths and monkeys in the forest canopy.
Birds of prey by weight.Andean condor: With a wingspan of around 3 m, it can soar for hours without flapping, riding the thermals above the Andes.

Tricky animal numbers.Blowholes on a sperm whale: Its single blowhole sits off to the left of its head, unlike the twin blowholes of baleen whales.
Tricky animal numbers.Blowholes on a humpback whale: Baleen whales, unlike toothed whales, have two blowholes, and a humpback's breath can be heard from far away.
Tricky animal numbers.Hearts in an octopus: It has three hearts: two pump blood to the gills and one to the body, and the main heart stops when it swims.
Tricky animal numbers.Hearts in a hagfish: The hagfish has a main heart plus three accessory pumps, and it can tie itself in a knot and produce huge amounts of slime.
Tricky animal numbers.Heart pairs in an earthworm: It has five pairs of aortic arches that act as hearts, though this blind burrower has no lungs and breathes through skin.
Tricky animal numbers.Muscles in a cat's ear: Each ear has 32 muscles, so a cat can rotate them nearly 180 degrees to pinpoint sounds.
Tricky animal numbers.Teeth in a giant armadillo: The giant armadillo has more teeth than most land mammals, with up to about 100, and digs burrows big enough for a person.
Tricky animal numbers.Eggs a queen bee lays per day: A queen bee may lay up to around 1,500 eggs on a good day, which can weigh more than she does.
Tricky animal numbers.Taste buds on a catfish: Catfish are covered with taste buds, so they can taste with their whole body and find food in murky water.
Tricky animal numbers.Sea otter hairs per sq inch: The densest fur of any animal keeps sea otters warm, since they have no blubber layer.

When these tech companies were founded.IBM: It began as the Computing-Tabulating-Recording Company and took the name International Business Machines in 1924.
When these tech companies were founded.Hewlett-Packard: A coin toss in a Palo Alto garage decided whose name came first.
When these tech companies were founded.Intel: Robert Noyce and Gordon Moore chose a name from 'integrated electronics'.
When these tech companies were founded.Microsoft: Bill Gates and Paul Allen founded it in Albuquerque, New Mexico, and the name means microcomputer software.
When these tech companies were founded.Apple: It was founded on April Fools' Day, and co-founder Ronald Wayne sold his share for $800 within weeks.
When these tech companies were founded.Oracle: It took its name from a CIA project that Larry Ellison had worked on.
When these tech companies were founded.Cisco: The name is short for San Francisco, and the logo echoes the Golden Gate Bridge.
When these tech companies were founded.Nvidia: The name draws on 'invidia', Latin for envy, and the company grew from graphics chips to AI hardware.
When these tech companies were founded.Netflix: It started by mailing DVDs, long before the company moved to streaming.
When these tech companies were founded.OpenAI: It began as a nonprofit, with co-founders including Sam Altman and Elon Musk.

When these American landmarks were compl.The White House: Designed by James Hoban, burned by the British in 1814, and officially named the White House by Theodore Roosevelt in 1901.
When these American landmarks were compl.US Capitol dome: Work on the cast-iron dome continued through the Civil War because Lincoln insisted it show the Union would endure.
When these American landmarks were compl.Brooklyn Bridge: Washington Roebling got caisson disease and his wife Emily oversaw construction; elephants walked across in 1884 to prove it was safe.
When these American landmarks were compl.Statue of Liberty: A gift from France, its copper skin is only about 2.4 mm thick and turned green with age.
When these American landmarks were compl.Lincoln Memorial: It has 36 columns for the states at Lincoln's death, and it was the setting of Martin Luther King's 1963 speech.
When these American landmarks were compl.Hoover Dam: Built in under five years, ahead of schedule, creating Lake Mead.
When these American landmarks were compl.Mount Rushmore: Gutzon Borglum led the carving, with dynamite, from 1927 to 1941.
When these American landmarks were compl.Space Needle: Built in about a year for the 1962 Seattle World's Fair, at 605 feet.
When these American landmarks were compl.Gateway Arch: At 630 feet it is the tallest man-made monument in the US, as tall as it is wide.
When these American landmarks were compl.One World Trade Center: At 1,776 feet it nods to the year 1776, and it's the tallest building in the Western Hemisphere.

When these Disney songs debuted.Heigh-Ho: The Seven Dwarfs' work song comes from Disney's first full-length animated feature, Snow White.
When these Disney songs debuted.When You Wish Upon a Star: Jiminy Cricket sang it in Pinocchio, and it won the Oscar for Best Original Song and became Disney's signature tune.
When these Disney songs debuted.Bibbidi-Bobbidi-Boo: The fairy godmother's nonsense chant from Cinderella earned an Oscar nomination.
When these Disney songs debuted.The Bare Necessities: Baloo sang it in The Jungle Book, the last animated film Walt Disney personally supervised.
When these Disney songs debuted.Under the Sea: The Little Mermaid's calypso number won the Oscar for Best Original Song for Alan Menken and Howard Ashman.
When these Disney songs debuted.A Whole New World: The Aladdin duet won an Oscar and a Grammy, and became the first Disney song to top the Billboard Hot 100.
When these Disney songs debuted.Circle of Life: Elton John and Tim Rice wrote it, and its opening Zulu chant was by Lebo M.
When these Disney songs debuted.Let It Go: Robert Lopez, co-writer, became the first person to win an EGOT twice, with his wife, Kristen Anderson-Lopez.
When these Disney songs debuted.How Far I'll Go: Auli'i Cravalho was 14 when she was cast to sing this Moana song by Lin-Manuel Miranda.
When these Disney songs debuted.We Don't Talk About Bruno: The Encanto hit reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in early 2022, a rare feat for a Disney song since the 1990s.

When these stadiums opened.The Colosseum, Rome: The arena could hold around 50,000 spectators, and its opening games under Titus reportedly lasted 100 days.
When these stadiums opened.Lord's (current ground): Founder Thomas Lord moved it twice; the present ground has a slope of about 2.5 metres from one side to the other.
When these stadiums opened.Old Trafford: Manchester United's 'Theatre of Dreams' was badly damaged by German bombs in 1941.
When these stadiums opened.Fenway Park: The oldest ballpark in Major League Baseball, it's home to the 37-foot wall nicknamed the Green Monster.
When these stadiums opened.Wrigley Field: Its ivy-covered walls are famous, but it had no lights for night games until 1988.
When these stadiums opened.Maracanã: Built for the 1950 World Cup, it held close to 200,000 people for the final.
When these stadiums opened.Camp Nou: Barcelona's home, Europe's largest stadium, symbolises the club's motto 'Més que un club', 'more than a club'.
When these stadiums opened.Allianz Arena: Its outer shell of inflated panels can light up red, blue or white depending on which team is playing.
When these stadiums opened.Wembley (new stadium): Its great steel arch rises 133 metres, and it can be seen across London.
When these stadiums opened.Yankee Stadium (current): Built beside the original 'House That Ruth Built', which was demolished after its final season.

Norse creation myth, in story order.Ginnungagap, the void: Ginnungagap was the yawning gap between fire and ice, and the whole universe grew out of it in the Norse story.
Norse creation myth, in story order.Ymir forms from the ice: Ymir was the first giant, formed where the ice met the heat, and from his sweat more giants were born.
Norse creation myth, in story order.Audhumla the cow appears: Audhumla fed Ymir with her milk, and she kept herself alive by licking salty ice blocks.
Norse creation myth, in story order.Buri licked free of ice: Buri emerged as Audhumla licked a block of salty ice, and he became the grandfather of Odin.
Norse creation myth, in story order.Bor takes a giantess wife: Bor married Bestla, a giantess, and their sons became the first gods. It's the first mix of gods and giants.
Norse creation myth, in story order.Odin, Vili and Ve are born: Odin, Vili and Ve were the first Aesir gods, and in the Norse tradition Odin became the chief of the gods.
Norse creation myth, in story order.Ymir is slain: Odin and his brothers killed Ymir, and so much blood poured out it drowned nearly all the other frost giants.
Norse creation myth, in story order.The world made from Ymir: The gods made the earth from Ymir's flesh, the seas from his blood, the mountains from his bones, and the sky from his skull.
Norse creation myth, in story order.Ask and Embla created: Odin and his brothers made the first humans from trees found on the shore: Ask from an ash and Embla from an elm.
Norse creation myth, in story order.Asgard is built: Asgard was the fortress of the Aesir gods, and a giant builder reportedly almost finished its wall with the help of his horse.

Legendary April Fools' pranks.Color TV via nylon stocking: Swedish TV told viewers a nylon stocking over the screen would produce colour. Many people really tried it, and it is a classic of the genre.
Legendary April Fools' pranks.Jovian-Plutonian gravity: The BBC's Patrick Moore claimed a planetary alignment would briefly cut gravity, and listeners called to say they had floated. A cheerful myth.
Legendary April Fools' pranks.Island nation San Serriffe: The Guardian's supplement described a fake island nation with two main islands, Sans and Serriffe. Typographers got the joke first.
Legendary April Fools' pranks.Big Ben goes digital: The BBC said the clock was going digital, with hands being replaced by a new display. Listeners phoned in to be assured.
Legendary April Fools' pranks.Sidd Finch, 168 mph pitcher: Sports Illustrated's George Plimpton wrote about a young Mets prospect who threw 168 mph and studied Zen. Many readers believed it, though the real record is about 105 mph.
Legendary April Fools' pranks.Nixon runs again: On NPR, a comic voice announced Richard Nixon was running again, with the slogan "I'm back." The imitation fooled some listeners.
Legendary April Fools' pranks.Taco Liberty Bell: Taco Bell took out full-page ads saying it had bought Philadelphia's Liberty Bell. Many people were outraged before the reveal.
Legendary April Fools' pranks.Left-Handed Whopper: Burger King ran an ad for a Whopper for left-handed people, with condiments rotated 180 degrees. Many customers really asked for it.
Legendary April Fools' pranks.BBC's flying penguins: The BBC clip showed penguins taking flight to winter in the tropics, narrated by Terry Jones. It remains one of the most-shared TV hoaxes.
Legendary April Fools' pranks.Pac-Man in Google Maps: Google Maps let you chase Pac-Man along real streets. The playable gag proved that April Fools' jokes could also be fun games.

From the garden: lightest to heaviest.Mustard seed: The parable of the mustard seed calls it the smallest of seeds, though some orchid seeds are in fact much smaller.
From the garden: lightest to heaviest.Grain of rice: Rice is a grass seed, domesticated in China over 9,000 years ago, and now feeds roughly half the world.
From the garden: lightest to heaviest.Pea: Gregor Mendel's experiments with pea plants in a monastery garden founded the science of genetics.
From the garden: lightest to heaviest.Garlic clove: Garlic is a relative of the onion, and ancient Egyptian pyramid builders reportedly ate it for strength.
From the garden: lightest to heaviest.Radish: One of the fastest-growing vegetables, it can be ready to pull in as little as three to four weeks.
From the garden: lightest to heaviest.Carrot: Early carrots were purple and yellow, and the orange kind became popular in the Netherlands in the 1600s.
From the garden: lightest to heaviest.Potato: Potatoes were first domesticated in the Andes, and there are thousands of varieties in Peru alone.
From the garden: lightest to heaviest.Eggplant: Botanically a berry and related to tomatoes, the eggplant belongs to the nightshade family.
From the garden: lightest to heaviest.Cabbage: It is the same species as broccoli, kale, cauliflower and Brussels sprouts: Brassica oleracea, bred into different shapes.
From the garden: lightest to heaviest.Pumpkin: Botanically a fruit, and record-weight pumpkins top 1,000 kg, grown by growers who feed them like athletes.

Disney's Moana, in story order.Gramma tells the legend: Moana (2016) drew on Polynesian voyagers, who crossed thousands of kilometres of Pacific using stars, swells and bird flight to find islands.
Disney's Moana, in story order.The ocean chooses little Moana: Auliʻi Cravalho was only 14 when she won the role of Moana, after a casting search that reached across Hawaii.
Disney's Moana, in story order.Gramma Tala dies: Tala returns as a glowing manta ray, an animal that Pacific peoples often saw as a link between humans and the sea.
Disney's Moana, in story order.Moana sets sail: Polynesians sailed double-hulled canoes and wayfinders navigated with no instruments, reading stars, waves and the flight of birds.
Disney's Moana, in story order.Moana finds Maui: Maui is a real figure of Polynesian myth, credited with fishing up islands and slowing the sun to lengthen the day.
Disney's Moana, in story order.Attack of the Kakamora: The coconut-armoured Kakamora come from Solomon Islands folklore, and the film turns them into pint-sized pirates on a tiny armada.
Disney's Moana, in story order.Tamatoa's lair: Tamatoa is a giant coconut crab, and real ones are the largest land-living arthropods, able to crack coconuts with their claws.
Disney's Moana, in story order.Te Kā cracks Maui's hook: Te Kā is a lava demon who was once the island goddess Te Fiti, and Maui's cracked hook shows how far he has fallen.
Disney's Moana, in story order.Maui flies off: Dwayne Johnson voiced Maui, and the tattoos that move and act as his conscience were hand-drawn by animators.
Disney's Moana, in story order.The heart goes back to Te Fiti: Lin-Manuel Miranda co-wrote the songs, including How Far I'll Go, which earned an Oscar nomination for Best Original Song.

Apollo 11's mission, in order.Saturn V launches: Saturn V is the most powerful rocket ever successfully flown, standing about 110 metres tall.
Apollo 11's mission, in order.Leaving Earth orbit: Trans-lunar injection sent the crew toward the Moon on a journey of about three days.
Apollo 11's mission, in order.Entering lunar orbit: Michael Collins stayed in orbit in Columbia, and is called the loneliest man in history.
Apollo 11's mission, in order.Eagle undocks from Columbia: Columbia and Eagle are the names of the command module and the lunar module.
Apollo 11's mission, in order.\"The Eagle has landed\": Eagle landed with less than a minute of fuel left, after an alarm flashed.
Apollo 11's mission, in order.Armstrong's first step: Armstrong said One small step for man; he said he meant to say a man.
Apollo 11's mission, in order.Planting the US flag: The flag was likely knocked over by Eagle's exhaust at lift-off, Buzz Aldrin later said.
Apollo 11's mission, in order.Eagle lifts off the Moon: Aldrin's pen was used as a switch when the ascent engine's circuit breaker broke.
Apollo 11's mission, in order.Splashdown in the Pacific: The USS Hornet picked up the crew, who were quarantined for weeks.
Apollo 11's mission, in order.Ticker-tape parade in NYC: New York held a ticker-tape parade for the astronauts on August 13, 1969.

Distance from the Sun.Mercury: Although closest, it isn't the hottest planet; with almost no atmosphere, its night side plunges to around minus 180 degrees Celsius.
Distance from the Sun.Venus: A thick carbon dioxide atmosphere makes it the hottest planet, at around 460 degrees Celsius, and it spins backward.
Distance from the Sun.Earth: Light from the Sun takes about eight minutes and twenty seconds to reach us, and this distance defines one astronomical unit.
Distance from the Sun.Mars: Its red color comes from iron oxide, rust, and it has the largest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons.
Distance from the Sun.Ceres: The largest object in the asteroid belt, it's also a dwarf planet, and it holds bright salt deposits in Occator Crater.
Distance from the Sun.Jupiter: Over a thousand Earths could fit inside it, and its Great Red Spot is a storm that has raged for centuries.
Distance from the Sun.Saturn: Its density is less than water's, so in theory, the planet would float in a bathtub big enough.
Distance from the Sun.Uranus: It rolls around the Sun tilted on its side, probably the result of an ancient collision, giving it extreme seasons lasting decades.
Distance from the Sun.Neptune: Discovered in 1846 through mathematical predictions rather than just observation, it has the fastest winds in the solar system.
Distance from the Sun.Pluto: Its distance varies greatly because its orbit is elliptical; it was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

Space exploration firsts.Sputnik 1: The Soviet satellite was a polished metal sphere about the size of a beach ball, and its beeping signal was heard worldwide.
Space exploration firsts.Explorer 1: America's first satellite carried an instrument that helped discover the Van Allen radiation belts around Earth.
Space exploration firsts.Gagarin in orbit: Yuri Gagarin's flight lasted 108 minutes, and he reportedly said 'Poyekhali!', or 'Let's go!', at launch.
Space exploration firsts.Tereshkova in orbit: Valentina Tereshkova, a textile worker and amateur parachutist, orbited Earth 48 times, and she remains the only woman to have flown solo.
Space exploration firsts.Leonov's spacewalk: Alexei Leonov's suit ballooned in the vacuum, and he had to let air out to squeeze back through the airlock.
Space exploration firsts.Salyut 1 station: The first space station was launched by the Soviets, but its first crew died returning home when their capsule lost pressure.
Space exploration firsts.Voyager 1 launched: It later became the first human-made object to enter interstellar space, and carries a golden record of Earth's sounds.
Space exploration firsts.Hubble launched: A flaw in its mirror blurred early images, and astronauts fixed it in 1993 with what was effectively a pair of glasses.
Space exploration firsts.ISS first module: The Russian-built Zarya module began a station that has been continuously inhabited since the year 2000.
Space exploration firsts.Crew Dragon's first crew: SpaceX's capsule was the first private spacecraft to carry NASA astronauts to the ISS, ending the reliance on Russian rockets.
